transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump is doing a final blitz of campaign rallies.
NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben reports Trump's messages have been mixed.
In recent rallies, the president has talked about admiring Ohio Senator John Hughes said
"but."
Last night in Lubbock, Texas, he criticized the press for covering those remarks.
And I made the mistake of saying that I started off by studying his ass.
Trump also riffed on a years old news story about Massachusetts Democratic Senator Elizabeth
Warren's heritage, and talked up the recent documentary about First Lady Melania Trump.
Republicans hope the president's involvement will turn out MAGA voters who might otherwise
stay home.
Trump's next stop is Ohio, and on Friday, he is scheduled to speak in Iowa.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
Yes, we can, Cesar Puedes.
Dolores Huerta, the woman behind the popular rallying cry for justice, has died.
She co-founded the United Farm Workers with Cesar Chavez to fight for labor protections
for the mostly Latino agricultural workforce, but she spent a lifetime championing the civil
rights of all historically marginalized people.
In 2019, NPR's Ted Radio Hour aired an excerpt from her TED Talk, in which she said the enemy
of social activism is apathy, especially among women.
You know, women, they have so many inhibitions.
Many of them have suffered so much trauma in their lives.
So many aggressions in their lives.
And so it's very hard for them to realize that they have leadership capacities, that
they can get out there and they can change the world.
This past March, Huerta shared traumatic chapters from her life in revealing that Chavez had
raped her more than half a century earlier when she was a young activist.
She said she never told because she was afraid it would harm the farm worker movement.
But she ended her statement telling readers, quote, "My silence ends here."
Dolores Huerta was 96 years old.
In Israel, the vast majority of votes have been counted.
In yesterday's election, there is still a deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
and his main challengers.
Here's NPR's Daniel Estrin.
The map could still shift as the rest of the votes are counted, but Netanyahu and his allies
so far have won 53 parliamentary seats. The center-right opposition block is trailing
behind Netanyahu with just 48 parliamentary seats.
Neither side has the 61-seat majority they'd need.
The main question is if the center-right opposition will break campaign promises and agree to
partner with Arab-led parties.
Arab parties so far have won a record 19 seats in parliament thanks to historically high
Arab voter turnout.
Netanyahu is claiming Arab parties, quote, "stole the elections," but it's not published
evidence.
It's an apparent attempt to prevent the opposition from partnering with Arab parties to unseat
him.
Next week, Israel's president will decide who to appoint to try to form a governing
coalition.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
This is NPR News.
The Federal Reserve is still expected to raise interest rates again this year, but not today.
At the conclusion of its two-day meeting, the Fed decided to hold rates steady days
ahead of the midterms, even though inflation is elevated.
Here's Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.
Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace.
While uncertainty remains, owing in part to geopolitical developments, domestic spending
has been resilient, productivity growth is strong, and capital investment robust.
While security officials have been warning for years that Chinese government hackers
might one day wreak havoc on U.S. critical infrastructure in the event of a conflict
like an invasion of Taiwan.
New research shows the lengths they're willing to go to to keep their hacking secret.
More from NPR's Jenna McLaughlin.
Mike Corca, a former FBI special agent, says he watched Chinese government hackers go to
great lengths to reach key targets and hide their activities.
By using previously undiscovered vulnerabilities, hacking into a long chain of virtual networks
and compromised devices like routers, every single time they wanted to reach a new target.
It definitely felt like a wild goose chase a lot of times.
Corca works with the Black Lotus Labs team at Lumen Technologies, a telecommunications
company that has a unique view of the flow of traffic along the backbone of the internet.
And he says he hopes to expose the Chinese government's playbook and shine a light on
Chinese strategic priorities, but also help defenders to shore up their systems from these
kinds of attacks.
Jen McLaughlin, NPR News.
U.S. stocks have ended the day mixed.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump's final campaign rallies draw mixed messages, including remarks about Senator John Hughes and Elizabeth Warren
Dolores Huerta, co-founder of the United Farm Workers, dies at age 96
Israel's election counted, Netanyahu and opposition deadlocked short of a 61-seat majority
Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady ahead of midterms despite elevated inflation
Chinese government hackers go to great lengths to conceal intrusions, according to new Lumen research
U.S. stocks end the day mixed
